chronology.market_state: registered causal state observed at the completed signal-date close and frozen for the trade

frozen_rules: Use the prior 250-session high already known at the signal; require that it remained unbroken for at least 60 completed market sessions.
Keep the exact first non-limit absorption breakout trigger and first legal next-open entry within three market sessions from the V1 mother; do not filter any chart manually.

Classify the signal date using only the registered causal BULL, BEAR, or TRANSITION state whose latest input is available by decision_at; never use future return, future breadth, calendar-year labels, or ex-post peaks/troughs.

In BULL use the original +20 percent target. In BEAR or TRANSITION use a +10 percent target, representing the shallower continuation opportunity visible in weak-state charts. Target execution remains no earlier than T+1.
If the target is not reached, retain the original H60 decision and execute only at the next legal sellable open; use 20 bp per side and no failure stop.
hypothesis: A stale-resistance absorption breakout has a deeper continuation opportunity when broad demand is causally strong, but in weak or transitional markets much of the available continuation is transient. State-routed profit realization may capture that transient opportunity without sacrificing bull-market convexity.

observations_that_generated_the_rule.important_non_rule: Do not use a causal-state admission filter; profitable charts occur in BULL, BEAR, and TRANSITION.
observations_that_generated_the_rule.review_scope: all 1047 twelve-month charts reviewed one by one before this rule was frozen
